24	## 1. Claude Code 能否自动把 session 对话和操作日志记录到项目 `logs/xxx.md`？
25	
26	**部分支持，但需要你自己用 hooks / export 脚本落地。**
27	
28	Claude Code 官方会持续保存 session，本地 transcript 默认在：
29	
30	```text
31	~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl
32	```
33	
34	也可以在会话里用 `/export` 把当前 conversation 保存为纯文本文件；官方文档还说明这些本地 session 文件默认 30 天后清理，可通过配置调整。([Claude Code][1])
35	
36	但是，**Claude Code 默认不会自动把完整对话保存到当前 repo 的 `logs/` 目录**。要做到这一点，推荐用 hooks。Claude Code hooks 能在 `SessionStart`、`UserPromptSubmit`、`PreToolUse`、`PostToolUse`、`Stop`、`SubagentStart/Stop`、`TaskCreated/Completed`、`SessionEnd` 等生命周期事件触发；hook 输入里包含 `session_id`、`cwd`、`transcript_path` 等信息。([Claude Code][2])
37	
38	你项目里其实已经有一个基础版本：`audit_event.py` 会从 hook stdin 读取 JSON payload，然后写到当前项目的 `.agent/audit/tool-events.jsonl`，字段包括 `timestamp`、`hook_event_name`、`tool_name`、`session_id`、`cwd` 和完整 payload。 这说明你的项目已经具备 **tool-event audit log**，但还没有完整的 **conversation transcript mirror / session summary log**。
39	
40	我建议分三层做：
41	
42	```text
43	.agent/audit/
44	  tool-events.jsonl              # raw hook events, 默认不提交或只提交 sanitized 样例
45	
46	logs/claude-sessions/
47	  <date>-<session-id>.jsonl       # transcript mirror，可选，不建议默认 commit
48	  <date>-<session-id>.summary.md  # curated session summary，可 review 后 commit
49	
50	docs/handoffs/
51	  m9-handoff.md
52	  m10-handoff.md                  # milestone 级别核心记忆，应该 commit
53	```
54	
55	关键安全建议：**不要默认把完整 transcript commit 到 GitHub**。Claude session 里可能包含本地路径、命令输出、错误日志、环境变量片段、PR 链接、甚至误打印的 secret。更好的做法是：
56	
57	```text
58	raw logs:
59	  .agent/audit/**
60	  logs/claude-sessions/raw/**
61	  默认 .gitignore
62	
63	curated memory:
64	  PROJECT_STATE.md
65	  docs/handoffs/*.md
66	  docs/adr/*.md
67	  docs/meeting-notes/*.md
68	  docs/evidence/*.md
69	  review 后 commit
70	```
71	
72	可以让 Claude Code 加一个 skill：
73	
74	```text
75	.claude/skills/session-closeout/SKILL.md
76	```
77	
78	用途是每次长任务结束后生成：
79	
80	```text
81	- What changed
82	- Files changed
83	- Tests run
84	- Decisions made
85	- Open questions
86	- Follow-up issues to create
87	- Memory updates proposed
88	```
89	
90	然后由 human 批准后更新 `PROJECT_STATE.md`、`docs/handoffs/`、ADR 或 GitHub issue。

94	## 2. Claude Code 支持 GitHub webhook 吗？能否响应 PR review / comments / labels？
95	
96	**支持几种不同层级，但要区分 “GitHub Actions 触发新 agent run” 和 “push 事件进入正在运行的本地 session”。**
97	
98	### 方案 A：GitHub Actions + `@claude`，最稳
99	
100	你现在已经有 `.github/workflows/claude.yml`，它监听：
101	
102	```yaml
103	issue_comment:
104	  types: [created]
105	pull_request_review_comment:
106	  types: [created]
107	issues:
108	  types: [opened, assigned]
109	pull_request_review:
110	  types: [submitted]
111	```
112	
113	并且只有 comment / issue / review body 包含 `@claude` 时才运行 Claude Code Action。 官方文档也确认 Claude Code GitHub Actions 可以通过 PR/issue 中的 `@claude` 触发，分析代码、创建 PR、实现功能和修 bug，并且 action 是基于 Claude Agent SDK 构建的。([Claude Code][3])
114	
115	这适合：
116	
117	```text
118	@claude review this PR
119	@claude implement issue #123
120	@claude summarize unresolved review comments
121	@claude update docs based on this decision
122	```
123	
124	如果你想让它更新 issue comments / labels / PR comments，workflow 权限需要从 read 扩到 write，例如：
125	
126	```yaml
127	permissions:
128	  contents: write
129	  pull-requests: write
130	  issues: write
131	  actions: read
132	  id-token: write
133	```
134	
135	但我建议分 workflow：
136	
137	```text
138	claude.yml
139	  手动 @claude 响应，允许 contents/pull-requests/issues write
140	
141	claude-code-review.yml
142	  自动 PR review，默认只读或只写 review comment
143	
144	issue-triage.yml
145	  label/comment triage，issues: write，但不改代码
146	
147	labels-sync.yml
148	  只同步 .github/labels.yml，需要人工 workflow_dispatch
149	```
150	
151	工程实践文档里的 AI pickup rule 很适合这里：implementation agent 只能处理 open issue、带 `ai:ready`、决策已 `decision:confirmed`、有 acceptance criteria、无 `ai:blocked`，且不涉及 secrets/破坏性 migration/生产 infra/客户可见副作用，除非 human 明确批准。
152	
153	### 方案 B：Claude Code Routines + GitHub trigger，云端事件触发
154	
155	Claude Code Routines 支持 schedule、API trigger、GitHub event trigger，运行在 Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure；GitHub trigger 会在匹配事件发生时启动一个新 session。([Claude Code][4]) 官方文档说明 GitHub triggers 当前支持 PR 和 release 两类事件，PR 事件包括 opened、closed、assigned、labeled、synchronized 等；每个匹配事件都会启动独立 session，不复用之前的 session。([Claude Code][4])
156	
157	这适合：
158	
159	```text
160	PR labeled ai:ready → 新 cloud session 生成 plan
161	PR updated → 自动 review diff
162	release created → 生成 release notes / readiness report
163	nightly → issue backlog grooming
164	```
165	
166	但它不适合保存“一个长期本地 session 的连续上下文”，因为每个 GitHub event 是新 session。你的 repo memory 仍然要靠 GitHub 文件和 issue/PR 记录。
167	
168	### 方案 C：Claude Code Channels，把 webhook 推进正在运行的本地 session
169	
170	Claude Code Channels 是另一类东西：它允许 MCP server 把 messages、alerts、webhooks 推入一个正在运行的 Claude Code session。官方说它可用于 CI results、chat messages、monitoring events，让 Claude 在你离开终端时也能反应；这是 research preview，需要 Claude Code v2.1.80+，并且 session 启动时要用 `--channels` opt-in。([Claude Code][5]) Channels reference 说明 channel 本质是 MCP server，通过 `notifications/claude/channel` 把外部事件送进 Claude Code session，可做 one-way webhook 或 two-way chat bridge。([Claude Code][6])
171	
172	这适合：
173	
174	```text
175	GitHub webhook → local channel server → active Arch Claude session
176	CI failed → Claude sees event immediately
177	Issue label changed → Claude receives payload
178	PR review submitted → Claude receives payload and responds
179	```
180	
181	但它更复杂，且是 research preview。我建议你的路线是：
182	
183	```text
184	短期：
185	  GitHub Actions @claude + issue labels/comments
186	
187	中期：
188	  Routines 处理 cloud-side GitHub event automation
189	
190	高级：
191	  Channels 将 selected GitHub webhook 推入正在运行的 Arch session
192	```

196	## 3. 如何从 GitHub comments 中提取需求确认/设计变更并沉淀为核心记忆？
197	
198	这件事不能让 Claude “看到评论就直接改 PROJECT_STATE”。应该用 **两阶段 memory promotion**：
199	
200	```text
201	GitHub comment/review/label event
202	  ↓
203	Issue Triage / Decision Extractor agent
204	  ↓
205	生成 proposed memory patch
206	  ↓
207	human review
208	  ↓
209	更新核心记忆文件
210	```
211	
212	我建议新增这些文件：
213	
214	```text
215	.claude/agents/github-decision-extractor.md
216	.claude/agents/github-issue-triage.md
217	.claude/agents/pr-review-followup.md
218	
219	.claude/skills/github-comment-distill/SKILL.md
220	.claude/skills/memory-promotion/SKILL.md
221	.claude/skills/pr-closeout-review/SKILL.md
222	```
223	
224	`github-comment-distill` 的职责：
225	
226	```text
227	输入：
228	  issue/PR comments, review comments, labels, PR diff, linked task doc
229	
230	输出：
231	  confirmed_requirements:
232	  changed_requirements:
233	  confirmed_design_decisions:
234	  changed_design_decisions:
235	  open_questions:
236	  blockers:
237	  proposed_labels:
238	  proposed_core_memory_patch:
239	```
240	
241	`memory-promotion` 的职责：
242	
243	```text
244	只生成 patch，不直接 claim truth：
245	- PROJECT_STATE.md patch
246	- docs/adr/xxxx.md draft
247	- docs/tasks/Mx-Txxx.md update
248	- docs/handoffs/mx-handoff.md update
249	- GitHub issue comment summary
250	```
251	
252	沉淀规则建议：
253	
254	```text
255	comment 只是 evidence，不自动成为 truth
256	label decision:confirmed + human 明确 wording 才能进入 ADR / PROJECT_STATE
257	模糊评论 → decision:needed + ai:blocked
258	实现细节 → task doc / PR closeout
259	长期架构决策 → ADR
260	milestone 状态 → PROJECT_STATE / docs/milestones.md
261	```
262	
263	这和你的工程实践文档一致：Issue Triage Agent 可以读 comments 并识别问题是否已解决，但不能从模糊评论推断决策；Implementation Agent 只能在确认后的 issue 上工作。

267	## 4. agents/skills 如何迁移到别的项目？
268	
269	**不要直接无脑复制到目标项目根目录。最佳方式是“staging → audit → adapt → install”。**
270	
271	Claude Code skills 是文件系统 artifact，项目级 skills 放在：
272	
273	```text
274	.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
275	```
276	
277	个人级 skills 放在：
278	
279	```text
280	~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
281	```
282	
283	官方文档说明 project skills 只对当前项目生效，personal skills 对所有项目生效，plugin skills 通过 plugin namespace 生效；skills 的 body 只在使用时加载，适合把重复流程从 `CLAUDE.md` 中拆出来。([Claude Code][7]) Agent SDK 也支持从 `.claude/skills/`、`~/.claude/skills/` 或 plugin 路径发现 filesystem skills。([Claude Code][8])
284	
285	我建议采用四层复用模型：
286	
287	### A. 通用、无项目耦合：做成 personal skill 或内部 plugin
288	
289	例如：
290	
291	```text
292	pr-closeout-review
293	github-comment-distill
294	session-closeout
295	ci-failure-triage
296	test-coverage-review
297	```
298	
299	可以放：
300	
301	```text
302	~/.claude/skills/
303	```
304	
305	或建立一个内部 repo：
306	
307	```text
308	kca-agent-pack/
309	  skills/
310	  agents/
311	  hooks/
312	  templates/
313	  README.md
314	```
315	
316	然后每个项目通过 submodule/subtree 或脚本安装。
317	
318	### B. 项目相关但可复用：先放 staging
319	
320	目标项目里先放：
321	
322	```text
323	.agent-import-staging/kca-agent-pack/
324	```
325	
326	然后让 Claude Code 执行：
327	
328	```text
329	Analyze .agent-import-staging/kca-agent-pack.
330	For each skill/agent:
331	- classify as reusable / needs adaptation / reject
332	- identify project-specific assumptions
333	- identify commands, paths, labels, policies to rewrite
334	- propose final installation path
335	Do not install until plan is approved.
336	```
337	
338	再迁移到：
339	
340	```text
341	.claude/skills/
342	.claude/agents/
343	docs/agent-practices/
344	```
345	
346	### C. 强项目耦合：不要迁移，只迁移理念
347	
348	例如 KCA 专用的 Kaggle approval、competition artifact layout、Supabase schema agent，不适合直接复制到普通 SaaS 项目。应该抽象出：
349	
350	```text
351	approval-gate-review
352	artifact-ledger
353	remote-side-effect-policy
354	```
355	
356	### D. 带脚本的 skills：必须安全审计
357	
358	官方 Agent Skills 文档提醒，Skills 可以包含指令和代码，恶意 Skill 可能诱导 Claude 执行不符合预期的工具或代码，所以只应使用可信来源的 skills。([Claude Platform][9]) 所以迁移时要检查：
359	
360	```text
361	- 是否调用 curl/wget/bash remote code
362	- 是否读取 .env / ssh / cloud credentials
363	- 是否 git push / deploy / delete
364	- 是否写绝对路径
365	- 是否假设某个 repo layout
366	- 是否修改 permissions/hooks
367	```

371	## 5. 产品 release 后是否还依赖 Claude Code？agents/skills/commands 底层调用什么？
372	
373	**KCA 产品 release 后不应该依赖 Claude Code CLI/desktop 本身。** Claude Code 是开发工具；KCA runtime 应该是你自己的 platform worker。
374	
375	你现在项目文档已经把两类 agent 区分得很清楚：Claude Code/VS Code/Desktop/Web 是 platform-development coding agents；runtime competition code agents 是平台内部启动的 agent，初始方向是 Claude Agent SDK、隔离 workspace/container、Kaggle Python/notebook-first、未来 model router 支持 Claude、GPT-style、local vLLM/Ollama 等。
376	
377	更进一步，你当前 M3 里已经把 runtime agent 方向改成了 provider-agnostic：`litellm.completion()` 作为统一 LLM provider interface，Claude、GPT-4o、本地 vLLM/Ollama 可按 job 选择。 这说明 KCA runtime **不是锁死在 Anthropic 模型上**。
378	
379	不过要分清楚几种能力来源：
380	
381	```text
382	Claude Code CLI skills/agents/hooks:
383	  用于开发 KCA repo；依赖 Claude Code。
384	
385	KCA .kca/skills or tools:
386	  你自己定义的产品 runtime skills/tools；不依赖 Claude Code。
387	
388	Claude Agent SDK:
389	  可以作为一种 runtime harness，提供 Claude Code-like agent loop、工具执行、context management。
390	
391	LiteLLM / OpenAI-compatible / vLLM / Ollama:
392	  可以作为 model provider；你要自己实现 tool loop 或通过 KCA worker adapter 接入。
393	
394	KCA commands:
395	  例如 kca run, kca decision, kca kaggle, kca skill；
396	  release 后就是你的产品 CLI/runtime API，不应该依赖 Claude Code。
397	```
398	
399	官方 Claude Agent SDK 的定位是“把 Claude Code 作为 library 构建生产 AI agents”，它提供相同的 tools、agent loop、context management，并且适合 CI/CD、custom applications、production automation。([Claude Code][10]) 但如果你使用 Agent SDK，它主要还是 Claude/Anthropic provider 体系；如果要接 vLLM/Ollama/OpenAI，你需要通过 KCA 的 model router / LiteLLM 路线来承接。
400	
401	我的建议：
402	
403	```text
404	产品 runtime 层：
405	  KCA Worker API
406	    - job runner
407	    - permission policy
408	    - tool executor
409	    - audit/event log
410	    - model router
411	    - GitHub adapter
412	    - Kaggle adapter
413	
414	可插拔 agent backend：
415	  - Claude Agent SDK backend
416	  - LiteLLM tool-loop backend
417	  - OpenAI Responses/Codex backend
418	  - Local vLLM/Ollama backend
419	```
420	
421	这样你可以先用 Claude Agent SDK 获得强 agentic coding 能力，后面逐步替换或混合其他模型。
422

425	## 6. 如何让 Claude Code 在 plan/design/architect 阶段更主动发现问题、提问和 debate？
426	
427	你观察得很对：Claude Code 有时会“按字面完成任务”，不会主动追问隐藏需求。例如你让它接手 `kkr.py/kkr.yaml`，它没有主动发现“多 Kaggle 账户提交”这种重要历史设计理念。其实你的 legacy 工具里已经有不少信号：`kkr.py` 支持 `--env` 覆盖 selected owner 的 dotenv path，`RunManifest` 里有 `owner`、`slug`、`env_path`，`kkr.yaml` 里也出现多个 Kaggle owner/kernel id，例如 `harrysun2006`、`firefly2006`。  
428	
429	要提高主动性，我建议建立一个 **Discovery / Debate Gate**，不是只靠“plan mode”。
430	
431	### 做法 1：每个迁移 legacy 的任务先跑 “design archaeology”
432	
433	新增 skill：
434	
435	```text
436	.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md
437	```
438	
439	要求 Claude 在实现前必须输出：
440	
441	```text
442	Legacy design archaeology:
443	1. What workflows does the legacy tool support?
444	2. What hidden assumptions exist?
445	3. What user personas/accounts exist?
446	4. What side effects exist?
447	5. What state files/registries exist?
448	6. What config dimensions exist?
449	7. Which features should be preserved?
450	8. Which features should be deprecated?
451	9. What questions must be asked before implementation?
452	10. What tests prove behavior parity?
453	```
454	
455	对 `kkr.py/kkr.yaml` 这种任务，强制它先识别：
456	
457	```text
458	- multi-account / owner / env mapping
459	- kernel push vs competition submit
460	- notebook submit vs local file submit
461	- run registry
462	- version labels
463	- fetch/watch/status/list lifecycle
464	- dry-run behavior
465	- H100 / docker_image / Kaggle metadata patch notes
466	```
467	
468	### 做法 2：在 task template 里加入 “assumption challenge”
469	
470	每个 architecture task 的 prompt 里固定加：
471	
472	```text
473	Before proposing implementation, challenge the task:
474	- What important requirement might be hidden in legacy files?
475	- What would break for an expert user?
476	- What design questions should be asked?
477	- What should be preserved even if not mentioned?
478	- What is the minimal reversible implementation?
479	- Give at least 3 alternative designs and argue tradeoffs.
480	```
481	
482	### 做法 3：增加反方 agent
483	
484	新增 agents：
485	
486	```text
487	.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md
488	.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md
489	.claude/agents/design-red-team.md
490	```
491	
492	`requirements-skeptic` 不写代码，只问问题。
493	`legacy-archaeologist` 只读 legacy scripts/configs，提取设计理念。
494	`design-red-team` 反驳当前方案，指出丢失能力和长期成本。
495	
496	### 做法 4：把“询问 human”变成 acceptance criteria
497	
498	例如：
499	
500	```text
501	Acceptance criteria:
502	- The agent identified at least 5 legacy behavior dimensions.
503	- The agent listed preserved / changed / dropped behaviors.
504	- The agent asked human for unresolved design decisions unless all are explicitly answered by docs/tests.
505	- No implementation starts until hidden assumptions are documented.
506	```
507	
508	这比“请主动一点”有效，因为它把主动性变成可检查输出。

511	
512	## 7. 你现在这些实践之外，还能怎么提高开发效率和准确率？
513	
514	你已经有一套很强的 workflow：
515	
516	```text
517	milestones/tasks + worktrees
518	Arch Linux Claude Code --bg 长跑
519	Mac VS Code 做短任务/review
520	mobile app remote control 批准/回答
521	GitHub issues/PR/comments/labels 作为第二交互界面
522	```
523	
524	我建议补齐下面 12 个实践。
525	
526	### 1. 给每个 task 增加 “evidence bundle”
527	
528	每个 PR 必须产出：
529	
530	```text
531	docs/evidence/<task-id>/
532	  closeout.md
533	  commands-run.txt
534	  test-results.md
535	  screenshots-or-traces-index.md
536	  decisions.md
537	```
538	
539	PR body 链接 evidence。工程实践文档也建议 logs 要总结到 issue，并把长期证据放在 `docs/evidence/` 或 GitHub artifact 中。
540	
541	### 2. 建立 “no silent memory” 机制
542	
543	每次 Claude Code 结束时强制问：
544	
545	```text
546	Does this task change project memory?
547	- no
548	- yes: propose patch to PROJECT_STATE.md / ADR / task doc / handoff
549	```
550	
551	只有 human approve 后才更新。
552	
553	### 3. 增加 PR Closeout bot
554	
555	每个 PR 自动检查：
556	
557	```text
558	- linked issue
559	- acceptance criteria checked
560	- tests run
561	- docs updated or not needed
562	- migrations/RLS/secrets impact
563	- remote side effects
564	- evidence link
565	```
566	
567	你的 engineering details 里已经建议 `pr-closeout-check.yml` 用于检查 PR body 是否包含 tests/docs/inventory/closeout links。
568	
569	### 4. 将 “labels” 变成状态机，而不只是标签
570	
571	建议状态流：
572	
573	```text
574	ai:triage
575	  → decision:needed + ai:blocked
576	  → decision:confirmed
577	  → ai:ready
578	  → ai:implementing
579	  → PR opened
580	  → review
581	  → merged / follow-up issues
582	```
583	
584	禁止：
585	
586	```text
587	ai:ready + decision:needed
588	ai:ready + ai:blocked
589	ai:implementing without owner/branch
590	```
591	
592	### 5. 引入 “issue-to-branch naming convention”
593	
594	例如：
595	
596	```text
597	issue #123
598	branch: claude/issue-123-short-title
599	worktree: .worktrees/issue-123-short-title
600	PR title: [#123] Short title
601	```
602	
603	这样 GitHub event、Claude session、worktree、logs、evidence 都能对齐。
604	
605	### 6. 为 Claude Code session 命名
606	
607	Claude Code 支持命名、resume、branch session；session picker 可以按当前 repo/worktree/branch 查找，并且可以导出 transcript。([Claude Code][1]) 你的长跑命令应统一：
608	
609	```bash
610	claude --bg \
611	  --name "M9-T002-spaceship-baseline-issue-123" \
612	  ...
613	```
614	
615	然后 log/evidence 也用同名 ID。
616	
617	### 7. 用 Channels 或 Remote Control 做“响应式开发”，但不要替代 GitHub Actions
618	
619	Remote Control 适合你现在用 mobile app 远程接管本地 session；官方说明 Remote Control 让本地 Claude Code session 继续运行在你的机器上，Web/mobile 只是窗口，适合从手机继续本地任务。([Claude Code][11])
620	
621	Channels 更适合把外部 webhook 推入本地 session。我的建议：
622	
623	```text
624	Remote Control:
625	  人主动介入、批准、回答问题。
626	
627	GitHub Actions:
628	  repo-native 事件、@claude、issue/PR 协作。
629	
630	Channels:
631	  高级事件流，例如 CI failed / PR labeled / issue assigned 推入正在跑的 Arch session。
632	```
633	
634	### 8. 让 KCA 自己 dogfood GitHub interface
635	
636	KCA 产品本身未来要能操作 GitHub，所以现在开发 KCA 时就用同一套抽象：
637	
638	```text
639	GitHub issue/comment/label event
640	  → KCA event adapter
641	  → decision extractor
642	  → job queue
643	  → worker/session
644	  → PR/comment/label update
645	  → audit log
646	```
647	
648	这样你不是“额外做 GitHub automation”，而是在 dogfood 产品核心能力。
649	
650	### 9. legacy migration 要有 behavior parity tests
651	
652	对 `kkr.py/kkr.yaml`，不要只迁移代码。要建立：
653	
654	```text
655	tests/fixtures/kkr/
656	  kkr.yaml
657	  minimal_notebook.ipynb
658	  fake_kaggle_api.json
659	
660	tests/test_kkr_parity.py
661	```
662	
663	覆盖：
664	
665	```text
666	- push --dry-run
667	- submit --dry-run
668	- watch/status/list/fetch parsing
669	- multi-owner env selection
670	- notebook vs local submit
671	- version label / registry behavior
672	```
673	
674	`kkr.py` 已经有 dry-run、JSON output、本地 registry、watch/status/list/fetch 等能力，适合做 parity suite。
675	
676	### 10. 对高风险任务使用双 agent review
677	
678	例如：
679	
680	```text
681	Agent A: implement
682	Agent B: review only
683	Agent C: test coverage reviewer
684	Human: final decision
685	```
686	
687	工程实践文档本身已经把 Inventory Drift Auditor、Issue Triage Agent、Implementation Planner、Implementation Agent、Milestone Reviewer、Test Coverage Reviewer、Release Readiness Agent 分成不同职责，并规定各自不能越权。
688	
689	### 11. 给 runtime worker 增加 replay
690	
691	每个 job 都能：
692	
693	```bash
694	kca job replay <job_id> --from-event <n> --dry-run
695	```
696	
697	这样当 agent 做错时，你可以复现：
698	
699	```text
700	input prompt
701	model/provider
702	tools allowed
703	tool calls
704	policy decisions
705	files changed
706	test results
707	human decisions
708	```
709	
710	M7 的目标里已经有 “permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny” 和 “audit log records every tool execution with policy decision”。 建议把它升级成可 replay 的 event sourcing。
711	
712	### 12. 明确 M9 前的 readiness gate
713	
714	你的 milestones 里 M9 是第一次真实 Kaggle end-to-end regression：Spaceship Titanic，目标是通过审批 gate 执行一次真实 `kaggle competitions submit` 并记录 public LB score。 所以 M9 前一定要 gate：
715	
716	```text
717	- CI green
718	- dry-run path green
719	- Kaggle credentials verified without printing
720	- submission.csv schema validated
721	- approval gate manually tested
722	- rollback / stop criteria documented
723	- logs/evidence path confirmed
724	```

845	## 总结建议
846	
847	你现在的方向是对的，但下一步要把“经验性流程”固化成产品机制：
848	
849	```text
850	Claude Code 开发侧：
851	  hooks + session closeout + GitHub Actions/Routines/Channels + agents/skills
852	
853	KCA runtime 侧：
854	  event log + model router + GitHub adapter + approval gate + replay + evidence bundle
855	
856	共同核心：
857	  GitHub repo 是 source of truth
858	  raw logs 不等于 memory
859	  human-confirmed decisions 才进入 PROJECT_STATE / ADR / milestones
860	```
861	
862	最优先做的不是 M9 继续堆功能，而是 **M8.6：session memory、GitHub event interface、legacy design archaeology、agent/skill reuse packaging**。这会直接提高后续 M9/M10 的开发效率和准确率。

```
1	# Platform-Development Coding Agents vs Runtime Competition Code Agents
2	
3	This document defines two related but distinct meanings of "code agent" used in this project. Confusing them leads to incorrect scope assumptions, unsafe tool use, and broken multi-tool workflows.
4	
5	## 1. Platform-development coding agents
6	
7	These are external AI tools used by the human developer to **build this repository**.
8	
9	Examples:
10	- Claude Code CLI, VS Code extension, Desktop app, or Web
11	- ChatGPT Pro / Codex
12	- Cursor
13	- Lovable (expected for UI shell later)
14	- GitHub Actions / Claude Code Routines for cloud automation
15	
16	Role:
17	- Write and review this product's source code and docs
18	- Update architecture decisions, task specs, and test configuration
19	- Run local tests, lint, and CI repair loops
20	- Open branches and PRs under human supervision
21	
22	Key constraint: **these tools do not share hidden memory across sessions or products.** The GitHub repository is the only reliable shared memory. Any decision that needs to survive a context reset must be written to repo files.
23	
24	## 2. Runtime competition code agents
25	
26	These are agents that the **finished platform** launches to help a human user compete.
27	
28	Initial runtime direction:
29	- Claude Agent SDK as the first core worker harness
30	- Isolated workspace or container per job
31	- Python / notebook-first for Kaggle workflows
32	- Future model router: Claude (Sonnet/Opus), GPT-style models, local vLLM/Ollama, specialist tools
33	
34	Runtime agents operate under competition-specific policy:
35	- Sandboxing and resource limits
36	- Budget and turn limits
37	- Human approval gates for remote side effects (Kaggle submissions, kernel pushes)
38	- Audit logging of every tool call and decision
39	
40	## Why this distinction matters
41	
42	| Concern | Platform-development agent | Runtime competition agent |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| Modifies this repo's source | Yes — primary job | No — modifies competition workspace |
45	| Needs GitHub push rights | Yes, under human approval | No — separate competition workspace |
46	| Runs in developer's terminal | Yes | No — isolated container/worker |
47	| Memory source | GitHub repo files | Competition workspace + Supabase records |
48	| Safety rules | `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/settings.json` | Competition policy module |
49	| Approval gates | Human reviews PRs, commits, pushes | Human approves Kaggle submissions, remote writes |
50	
51	## Rule
52	
53	When writing agent instructions, skills, hooks, or tool policies, always specify which agent type is in scope. Do not write rules that apply to both without making the dual-applicability explicit.
54	
```

````markdown
# GitHub as Agent Interface

Status: design note. Source: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §A1 questions 2, 3, and 7.

This document describes how GitHub issues, PRs, comments, reviews, and labels are used as a structured human / AI collaboration interface for KCA development, and how the same interface should be dogfooded by the KCA runtime later.

This doc is paired with [`session-memory-and-audit.md`](session-memory-and-audit.md), which covers how transcripts, tool events, and evidence are mirrored and curated. Together they replace the assumption that "Claude remembers" with "the repo remembers".

Scope: **platform-development coding agents** today (Claude Code CLI, VS Code extension, Routines, Actions). The same patterns are expected to be reused by the **KCA runtime** when it later operates on user-owned GitHub repos. See [`platform-vs-runtime-agents.md`](platform-vs-runtime-agents.md) for that distinction.

---

## 1. Why GitHub is the agent interface

The agent does not share hidden memory across sessions, machines, or products. The GitHub repo is the only reliable shared memory:

- `issues/` — the work backlog and decision log.
- `pulls/` — the change proposals + review trail.
- `comments` — the discussion thread, treated as evidence, not as truth.
- `labels` — the state machine that gates AI pickup.
- repo files (`PROJECT_STATE.md`, `docs/adr/`, `docs/milestones.md`, `docs/handoffs/`) — the curated memory that survives context resets.

The rule that follows from this: **a comment is evidence, not a decision.** Only an explicit human confirmation, captured in a labeled state transition or a repo-file change, promotes a comment into project memory. This is the principle behind the [memory-promotion workflow](session-memory-and-audit.md#3-memory-promotion-workflow).

---

## 2. Three trigger layers

GitHub-driven agent work happens at three different layers. Each has a different blast radius, cache lifetime, and security profile. Pick the layer per use case; do not collapse them.

| Layer | Mechanism | Session lifetime | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Actions `@claude` | `.github/workflows/claude.yml` + `claude-code-review.yml` | One workflow run per event | Explicit human-invoked tasks: `@claude review`, `@claude implement #123` |
| B. Routines (cloud) | Anthropic-managed cloud, GitHub PR/release triggers | One new session per matching event | Automated triage, PR-on-label, nightly grooming |
| C. Channels (research preview) | MCP channel server pushed into a running local session via `--channels` | Pushed into existing session | Wake a long-running Arch `--bg` session on CI failure / label change |

Today only A is in repo. B and C are roadmap items and should be added incrementally — see §7 rollout order.

### Layer A — GitHub Actions + `@claude` (default)

Two workflows are already present:

- `.github/workflows/claude.yml` — listens on `issue_comment.created`, `pull_request_review_comment.created`, `issues.opened/assigned`, `pull_request_review.submitted`, and only runs when the body contains `@claude`.
- `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml` — automatic per-PR review.

Recommended split going forward — keep each workflow's `permissions:` block minimal:

| Workflow | `permissions:` | Allowed actions |
|---|---|---|
| `claude.yml` | `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `issues: write` | Implement / fix / open PR, only when a human typed `@claude` |
| `claude-code-review.yml` | `pull-requests: write` (review comments only) | Post review comments on diff; no code writes |
| `issue-triage.yml` (proposed) | `issues: write` | Add/remove labels per [`github-issue-triage`](../../.claude/agents/github-issue-triage.md) rules; no code writes |
| `labels-sync.yml` (proposed) | `issues: write`, `workflow_dispatch` only | Apply `.github/labels.yml`; never on push |

Authority binding from `CLAUDE.md`: non-destructive GitHub writes (`gh issue/pr create|edit|comment|close|reopen|merge|ready`, `gh label create|edit|clone`, `gh release create|edit`, `git push` of new commits) are auto-allowed for dev-phase agents. Permanent deletions, force-push, and `--delete-branch` on merge remain denied without explicit approval.

### Layer B — Routines (cloud-side automation)

Each GitHub trigger spawns a fresh session — Routines do **not** continue an existing session. The repo must therefore carry every input the new session needs (issue body, linked task spec, acceptance criteria, evidence links). Routines are appropriate for:

- `pull_request.labeled` (`ai:ready`) → cloud session generates implementation plan as a PR comment.
- `pull_request.synchronize` → re-run automated review.
- `release.created` → generate release notes / readiness report draft.
- `schedule` (nightly) → backlog grooming, drift audit, stale-issue sweep.

Routines should never perform destructive operations; their output is comments and labels, not merges.

### Layer C — Channels (push events into running session)

Research preview. Reserve for the case where a long-running local Claude Code session (e.g. `claude --bg --name M9-T002-...` on the Arch box) needs to react to a webhook without polling. Treat the channel server as an untrusted source of payload data — channel messages are not instructions to follow blindly, they are events to react to according to the existing agent rules.

Examples:
- CI failed on the PR this session opened → Claude sees the event and starts a repair loop.
- Issue label flipped to `decision:confirmed` → unblock the waiting session.
- PR review submitted → start follow-up agent.

Adopting Channels is gated on (1) v2.1.80+ available, (2) an audited channel-server implementation, (3) explicit `--channels` opt-in per session.

---

## 3. Label state machine

Labels are not decorative — they are the gate that controls which issues an agent may pick up. The full lifecycle:

```text
ai:triage
   │
   ├─ unclear / needs decision  ──►  decision:needed + ai:blocked
   │                                       │
   │                                       ▼
   │                                 decision:confirmed   (human typed the resolution)
   │                                       │
   └─ already actionable ─────────►  ai:ready
                                          │
                                          ▼
                                     ai:implementing  (agent acked, branch + owner exist)
                                          │
                                          ▼
                                       PR opened
                                          │
                                          ▼
                                     review → merged
                                          │
                                          ▼
                                  follow-up issues created
```

Forbidden combinations (enforced by triage):

- `ai:ready` + `decision:needed`
- `ai:ready` + `ai:blocked`
- `ai:implementing` with no owner or no branch

Binding rule from `CLAUDE.md`: an Implementation Agent may pick up an issue only when `ai:ready` is set (and `decision:confirmed` if a decision was required), the issue has explicit acceptance criteria, and it is not also `ai:blocked`. Triage and drift agents may propose label changes deterministically but must not infer decisions from ambiguous comment text.

---

## 4. Issue / branch / worktree / PR naming

Adopt one identifier per unit of work, so GitHub events, Claude sessions, worktrees, logs, and evidence bundles all align:

```text
issue            #123
branch           claude/issue-123-short-title
worktree         .claude/worktrees/issue-123-short-title
session name     M9-T002-short-title-issue-123
PR title         [#123] Short title
evidence dir     docs/evidence/issue-123/
```

The session name is the join key for the [audit & memory layer](session-memory-and-audit.md). Always pass `--name` when starting a `--bg` session.

---

## 5. Comment-to-memory pipeline

The mechanism that promotes a comment into project memory is two-phase, never single-step:

```text
GitHub event (comment / review / label)
        │
        ▼
github-comment-distill skill            (read-only; produces a structured draft)
        │
        ▼
proposed memory patch
  - PROJECT_STATE.md diff
  - docs/adr/<n>.md draft
  - docs/tasks/<id>.md update
  - docs/handoffs/m{N}-handoff.md update
  - GitHub issue summary comment
        │
        ▼
human review (label transition or PR approval)
        │
        ▼
memory-promotion skill applies the patch and commits
```

The distill skill's required output schema:

```yaml
confirmed_requirements:        # explicit, with quoted evidence + comment URL
changed_requirements:          # before / after, with evidence
confirmed_design_decisions:
changed_design_decisions:
open_questions:                # → decision:needed
blockers:                      # → ai:blocked
proposed_labels:               # add / remove
proposed_core_memory_patch:    # unified diff against repo files
```

Promotion rules — these are the load-bearing constraints, enforced by the agent definition, not by code:

1. A comment is evidence, never truth.
2. Only `decision:confirmed` + explicit human wording promotes a comment into an ADR or `PROJECT_STATE.md`.
3. Ambiguous comments → `decision:needed` + `ai:blocked`; the agent asks rather than infers.
4. Implementation detail → task doc / PR closeout, not ADR.
5. Long-term architecture decision → ADR (`docs/adr/`).
6. Milestone status → `PROJECT_STATE.md` + `docs/milestones.md`.

Existing repo references that already implement parts of this contract: [`.claude/agents/github-issue-triage.md`](../../.claude/agents/github-issue-triage.md), [`.claude/agents/pr-review-followup.md`](../../.claude/agents/pr-review-followup.md), [`.claude/skills/pr-closeout-review/`](../../.claude/skills/pr-closeout-review/).

---

## 6. Required agents and skills

| File | Type | Responsibility | Must not |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.claude/skills/github-comment-distill/SKILL.md` | skill | Read issue/PR/review/label payload, emit structured draft per §5 schema | Write to repo files; infer decisions from ambiguous text |
| `.claude/skills/memory-promotion/SKILL.md` | skill | Apply approved memory patch to `PROJECT_STATE.md` / ADR / task doc | Apply without an explicit confirmation marker (label or approval) |
| `.claude/skills/pr-closeout-review/SKILL.md` | skill (exists) | Verify PR body checklist: linked issue, acceptance criteria, tests, docs, evidence, schema, remote side effects | Auto-merge |
| `.claude/agents/github-decision-extractor.md` | agent | Run the distill skill over a window of comments | Edit code |
| `.claude/agents/github-issue-triage.md` | agent (exists) | Propose label/comment changes deterministically | Grant `ai:ready` without `decision:confirmed` |
| `.claude/agents/pr-review-followup.md` | agent (exists) | Summarize unresolved review comments | Resolve threads by guessing intent |

The "Must not" column is enforced by the agent body itself — see `docs/engineering-practice.md` for the broader role boundaries (Inventory Drift Auditor, Implementation Agent, Milestone Reviewer, Release Readiness Agent).

---

## 7. Rollout order

This is the planning input for the M8.6 "GitHub event + session memory hardening" track suggested in the meeting notes.

1. **Now** — Actions layer hardening: split workflow permissions per §2, add `issue-triage.yml`, keep `labels-sync.yml` `workflow_dispatch`-only.
2. **Next** — Comment-to-memory pipeline: ship `github-comment-distill` and `memory-promotion` skills and the `github-decision-extractor` agent; wire them into the triage workflow as proposal-only.
3. **Then** — Routines for `pull_request.labeled` (`ai:ready`) and nightly backlog grooming.
4. **Later** — Channels opt-in for the Arch `--bg` session, gated on v2.1.80+ and an audited channel server.
5. **Eventually** — KCA runtime reuses the same adapter to operate on user repos: `GitHub event → KCA event adapter → decision extractor → job queue → worker → PR/comment/label update → audit log`.

---

## 8. Non-goals

- Replacing PR review with autonomous merging — every merge still requires human approval.
- Storing transcripts in-repo — see [`session-memory-and-audit.md`](session-memory-and-audit.md) §2 for why raw transcripts stay out of git.
- Allowing agents to mutate labels on issues they themselves opened without a separate reviewer.
- Cross-repo automation — this design covers `tt_pangu` only; KCA-runtime reuse on user repos is a future milestone, not a current scope.

---
````

````markdown
# GitHub as Agent Interface

Status: design note. Source: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §A1 questions 2, 3, and 7.

This document describes how GitHub issues, PRs, comments, reviews, and labels are used as a structured human / AI collaboration interface for KCA development, and how the same interface should be dogfooded by the KCA runtime later.

This doc is paired with [`session-memory-and-audit.md`](session-memory-and-audit.md), which covers how transcripts, tool events, and evidence are mirrored and curated. Together they replace the assumption that "Claude remembers" with "the repo remembers".

Scope: **platform-development coding agents** today (Claude Code CLI, VS Code extension, Routines, Actions). The same patterns are expected to be reused by the **KCA runtime** when it later operates on user-owned GitHub repos. See [`platform-vs-runtime-agents.md`](platform-vs-runtime-agents.md) for that distinction.

---

## 1. Why GitHub is the agent interface

The agent does not share hidden memory across sessions, machines, or products. The GitHub repo is the only reliable shared memory:

- `issues/` — the work backlog and decision log.
- `pulls/` — the change proposals + review trail.
- `comments` — the discussion thread, treated as evidence, not as truth.
- `labels` — the state machine that gates AI pickup.
- repo files (`PROJECT_STATE.md`, `docs/adr/`, `docs/milestones.md`, `docs/handoffs/`) — the curated memory that survives context resets.

The rule that follows from this: **a comment is evidence, not a decision.** Only an explicit human confirmation, captured in a labeled state transition or a repo-file change, promotes a comment into project memory. This is the principle behind the [memory-promotion workflow](session-memory-and-audit.md#3-memory-promotion-workflow).

---
````

````markdown
# Session Memory and Audit

Status: design note. Source: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §A1 questions 1 and 7.

This document describes how a Claude Code session's conversation, tool calls, and produced evidence are mirrored, audited, and selectively promoted into curated project memory. It is paired with [`github-as-agent-interface.md`](github-as-agent-interface.md), which describes the GitHub side of the same collaboration model.

The guiding principle: **raw logs are not memory.** Raw transcripts and tool-event streams capture *what happened*; curated repo files (`PROJECT_STATE.md`, ADRs, milestone docs, handoffs, evidence bundles) capture *what the project knows*. The promotion step between them is always gated by a human decision.

Scope: **platform-development coding agents** (Claude Code CLI / VS Code / Desktop / Routines / Actions) building this repository. The same three-layer model is the target for the KCA runtime's job audit log when KCA goes live — see [`platform-vs-runtime-agents.md`](platform-vs-runtime-agents.md).

---

## 1. The three storage tiers

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Tier 1 — raw                          (machine-readable, not committed)      │
│   .agent/audit/tool-events.jsonl          ← hook stdin payloads              │
│   logs/claude-sessions/raw/*.jsonl        ← transcript mirror (optional)     │
│   ~/.claude/projects/<project>/*.jsonl    ← Claude Code's own session store  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼  session-closeout skill
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Tier 2 — curated session                 (human-reviewable, optional commit) │
│   logs/claude-sessions/<session>.summary.md                                   │
│   docs/evidence/<task-id>/closeout.md                                         │
│   docs/evidence/<task-id>/commands-run.txt                                    │
│   docs/evidence/<task-id>/test-results.md                                     │
│   docs/evidence/<task-id>/decisions.md                                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼  memory-promotion skill (human approval)
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Tier 3 — core memory                              (committed; source of truth)│
│   PROJECT_STATE.md                                                           │
│   docs/adr/<n>-<slug>.md                                                     │
│   docs/milestones.md                                                         │
│   docs/handoffs/m{N}-handoff.md                                              │
│   docs/m{N}-final-review.md                                                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

A datum can only move down the page, never sideways. Tier 1 → Tier 2 is automated. Tier 2 → Tier 3 requires a human-confirmed decision (a label transition, a PR approval, or explicit wording in a comment); see [`github-as-agent-interface.md`](github-as-agent-interface.md#5-comment-to-memory-pipeline).

---

## 2. Tier 1 — raw logs

### 2.1 What exists today

- **Tool-event audit:** `.claude/hooks/audit_event.py` is registered as a hook handler. It reads the hook stdin payload and appends to `.agent/audit/tool-events.jsonl`. Fields: `timestamp`, `hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `session_id`, `cwd`, full payload. This covers `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, and other lifecycle events that Claude Code emits.
- **Tool guard:** `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` enforces deny-rules before tool execution. Its decisions should be recorded into the same audit stream (see §6 next steps).
- **Claude Code's own transcript:** the CLI persists each session as `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl` and rotates after 30 days by default. This is per-host and not in the repo.

### 2.2 What to add

A new helper `scripts/claude_export_session.py` mirrors a finished session into `logs/claude-sessions/raw/<session>.jsonl` and emits a curated summary alongside it. It must:

```text
input:
  hook payload providing transcript_path and session_id

output:
  logs/claude-sessions/raw/<session-id>.jsonl       (Tier 1, gitignored)
  logs/claude-sessions/<session-id>.summary.md      (Tier 2, reviewable)

redaction (mandatory before any write):
  - .env / .env.local / .env.development contents
  - ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json (username + key)
  - SSH keys, AWS / gcloud credentials, gh OAuth token
  - any value matching configured secret patterns
```

The dev-phase secret policy in `CLAUDE.md` permits the agent to read project `.env` and `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json` *for use*, but never to copy that content into web fetches, public PRs, comments, **or exported logs**. The exporter is the enforcement point.

### 2.3 What stays out of git

`.gitignore` already excludes `.agent/` and should be extended to cover the raw subtree:

```gitignore
.agent/
logs/claude-sessions/raw/
```

Raw transcripts may contain local paths, command outputs, error messages, environment-variable fragments, PR URLs, and accidentally-printed secrets. Default policy: **do not commit them.** A sanitized fixture, used for tests of the exporter and the distill skills, is the only acceptable in-repo example.

---

## 3. Tier 2 — curated session and evidence

### 3.1 Session closeout

A new skill `.claude/skills/session-closeout/SKILL.md` runs at the end of any non-trivial session. Required output sections:

```text
- What changed                  (files / commands / artifacts)
- Files changed                 (paths only, no diffs)
- Tests run                     (command + result)
- Decisions made                (with quoted evidence)
- Open questions                (→ decision:needed if any)
- Follow-up issues to create
- Memory updates proposed       (Tier 3 patch draft; not applied)
```

The closeout is written to `logs/claude-sessions/<session-id>.summary.md`. The session name (see [`github-as-agent-interface.md`](github-as-agent-interface.md#4-issue--branch--worktree--pr-naming)) is the join key — issue, branch, worktree, evidence dir, and summary all share it.

### 3.2 Evidence bundle per task / PR

Every non-trivial PR carries an evidence bundle:

```text
docs/evidence/<task-id>/
  closeout.md                 ← human-readable summary, used as PR body source
  commands-run.txt            ← exact commands, copy-paste reproducible
  test-results.md             ← test output excerpts, pytest IDs, metrics
  screenshots-or-traces-index.md
  decisions.md                ← what was decided and why; cites issue / comment
```

The PR body links the evidence dir and ticks the checklist in `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The `pr-closeout-review` skill verifies the bundle exists and the checklist boxes have supporting evidence — it does not auto-merge.

### 3.3 "No silent memory" rule

Every session closeout must answer one explicit question:

```text
Does this task change project memory?
  - no   → done.
  - yes  → propose Tier 3 patch (see §4). Do not apply.
```

A "yes" with no patch, or an applied patch with no human approval, are both contract violations.

---

## 4. Tier 3 — core memory

Tier 3 files are the project's source of truth. They survive context resets, session terminations, machine swaps, and product handovers. Composition:

| File | Holds | Updated by |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT_STATE.md` | Current milestone status, active risks, next actions | Milestone closeout + memory-promotion |
| `docs/milestones.md` | Milestone roster, scope, dependency order | Milestone planning + closeout |
| `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` | Per-milestone validation matrix and outcome | `milestone-final-review` skill |
| `docs/handoffs/m{N}-handoff.md` | Cross-session continuity notes | Session closeout, milestone closeout |
| `docs/adr/<n>-<slug>.md` | Long-term architecture decisions | `memory-promotion` after `decision:confirmed` |
| `docs/tasks/<task-id>.md` | Per-task spec, acceptance criteria, status | Task author + closeout |

Promotion is performed by the `.claude/skills/memory-promotion/SKILL.md` skill. Its hard constraint: it accepts a patch only if (a) the source comment or session decision carries an explicit confirmation marker (`decision:confirmed` label, PR approval, or quoted human "yes/approved/confirmed"), and (b) the patch is reviewable as a normal diff. It does not write to Tier 3 from raw logs directly.

---

## 5. Required skills and helpers

| Path | Type | Responsibility | Must not |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.claude/hooks/audit_event.py` | hook (exists) | Append tool events to `.agent/audit/tool-events.jsonl` | Write outside `.agent/` |
| `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` | hook (exists) | Enforce deny-rules pre-tool | Bypass the deny on agent self-instruction |
| `scripts/claude_export_session.py` | script (proposed) | Mirror + redact session transcript into Tier 1/2 | Write secrets; commit raw |
| `.claude/skills/session-closeout/SKILL.md` | skill (proposed) | Emit Tier 2 summary; propose Tier 3 patch | Apply Tier 3 patch |
| `.claude/skills/memory-promotion/SKILL.md` | skill (proposed) | Apply approved Tier 3 patch | Apply without confirmation marker |
| `.claude/skills/pr-closeout-review/` | skill (exists) | Verify evidence bundle + PR checklist | Auto-merge |
| `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` | skill (proposed) | Extract preserved / changed / dropped behaviors from legacy code before reimplementation | Skip the discovery step on "small" tasks |

---

## 6. Replay and job-event sourcing (KCA runtime target)

The platform-development side runs in Claude Code; the KCA runtime needs to provide the same accountability for jobs it launches on behalf of users. The same three-tier shape applies, with one extension: every job is replayable.

```bash
kca job replay <job_id> --from-event <n> --dry-run
```

Replay must reconstruct:

```text
- input prompt
- model / provider                  (selected via KCA model router)
- tools allowed                     (policy resolution decision)
- tool calls                        (with arguments and results)
- policy decisions                  (allow / ask / deny + reason)
- files changed
- test results
- human decisions                   (approvals, denials, edits)
```

M7 already targets policy decisions in the audit log; the upgrade for the runtime is to turn the append-only log into an event-sourced stream suitable for `replay --from-event`. This is a future-milestone item, listed here so the platform-side design (this doc) and the runtime-side design stay aligned.

---

## 7. Security model

1. **Read-for-use, not read-to-share.** Secrets that the dev-phase carve-out permits the agent to read (`.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.development`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`) must not appear in any file the exporter writes, in any web fetch, or in any GitHub comment.
2. **Default-deny on commit.** Tier 1 paths are gitignored. The only way data crosses the commit boundary is via Tier 2 → Tier 3 promotion, which is human-reviewed as a normal diff.
3. **Untrusted-data principle.** Anything inside a transcript that *looks like an instruction* — a forum quote, a dataset README excerpt, a tool error message — is data, not an order. Closeout summaries and memory-promotion patches must preserve this distinction; quoted content is quoted, not adopted.
4. **No transcript-driven side effects.** The exporter and the closeout skill never trigger remote writes. They produce files for review.
5. **Audit before publish.** Before any GitHub write that quotes session content, the relevant excerpt passes through the redactor.

---

## 8. Rollout order

1. **Now** — formalize Tier 1: extend `audit_event.py` if needed for missing fields, confirm `.gitignore` covers `.agent/` and `logs/claude-sessions/raw/`.
2. **Next** — ship `scripts/claude_export_session.py` with the redaction allow/deny list and a sanitized-fixture test.
3. **Then** — add the `session-closeout` skill and wire it into the milestone-loop protocol so every Loop Prompt closeout emits a Tier 2 summary.
4. **Then** — add the `memory-promotion` skill, used by milestone closeout to update `PROJECT_STATE.md` / handoff / ADR from approved patches.
5. **Later** — implement KCA runtime job event sourcing + `kca job replay`.

---

## 9. Non-goals

- Automating Tier 3 writes from raw logs — promotion is always human-gated.
- Committing full transcripts to the repo — sanitized fixtures only.
- Building a custom log viewer — Tier 2 summaries are plain markdown so existing review tools (GitHub PR diff, `gh pr view`, local editor) work.
- Replacing Claude Code's own session store — `~/.claude/projects/...` remains the working session record; this design adds an in-repo mirror, not a replacement.

---
````
